reason: The Control Tower limits page (and its registration troubleshooting page) now says ten SCPs per OU, which matches the newest relevant change, the 2026-05-15 Organizations SCP quota raise from 5 to 10 per node; the 'all policy limits are hard limits' note is on the current Organizations quotas page. No change item or corpus text gives a newer value (only an older SRA prescriptive page still says 5).

The newest relevant change is the 2024-05-20 raise of concurrent control operations to 100, which the claim states; later items (Config rules, Security Hub controls, controls-dedicated experience, LZ 4.0, PrivateLink) add controls or features but do not change the concurrency limit, and the current limits page still says 100.

The 2022-12-16 change introduced 5 concurrent account operations; the current limits page, the Account Factory page and the quota-increase page all say default 5, adjustable, maximum 10, and the unmanage one-at-a-time rule is on the current limits page. The 2026 AFT item about re-applying customizations does not change these quotas.

The claim and its condition date the optional CloudTrail integration to landing zone 4.0, but the current Control Tower guide says the opt-out of Control Tower-managed trails arrived with landing zone 3.0 (release notes for 3.0, 2022-07-29; 'When you update your landing zone to version 3.0 or later, you can choose to opt into or opt out of organization-level CloudTrail trails'); 4.0 only reshaped it as an optional service integration. Also, on opt-out Control Tower 'still creates the trail, but sets its status to Off'. The history the claim teaches is misdated. See full:controltower-userguide lines 17744-17747 and 4605.

The claim restates the 2025-11-19 What's New item itself; later Organizations items (Path field, backup policies, SCP and RCP quotas, CloudTrail membership events, departure security controls, GuardDuty policies) do not reverse or replace direct transfers, and a corpus search finds no conflicting statement.

The claim restates the 2026-07-22 item, the newest RCP quota change; the only later Organizations item (GuardDuty policies, 2026-09-25) does not touch RCP quotas and the corpus has no newer RCP number. Writers should note it went live after 2026-07-15, so it is not examinable yet.
The 2023-06-08 raise from 20 to 250 is the newest pending-invitation change; the current General Reference quota table shows 250 and adjustable, and later RAM items only add shareable resource types.

The 2024-10-30 item added security group sharing; the current shareable-resources table still marks security groups as shareable with only accounts in the same organization, and later RAM items (CloudFront VPC origins, Cloud Map, EBS volumes, EventBridge buses, SSM documents) do not change security group sharing.

The current RAM service quotas page and General Reference both give 250 (adjustable), sending-account only, no receiving-account quota, no invitations inside an organization with sharing turned on; the newest relevant change is the 2023-06-08 raise to 250 and later items only add resource types.
